# OWL ontology: what DISL cannot express

This file accompanies [w3c-owl.dis](w3c-owl.dis), the DISL specification of the OWL ontology diagram (`w3c/owl`, OWL 2 ontologies stored as Turtle `.ttl` or N-Triples `.nt`). The `.dis` says what DISL can say: the element and relation types, the VOWL-style notation, the toolbox, the inspector forms, the findings as constraints, the refusals DISL has a place for, and where persistence and layout hand over to plugins. This file holds everything else: how triples become drawn elements, how anonymous class expressions are identified and labelled, the layout algorithm, the interaction details and refusal sentences, the places where the implementation and its removed specification differ, and what DISL 0.1 could not say. Each point names the code, specification or conversation that shows it.

Backend paths below are relative to `src/diagrams/rdf/backend/EtAlii.Adp.Diagram.Rdf/`, test paths to `src/diagrams/rdf/backend/EtAlii.Adp.Diagram.Rdf.Tests/` and client paths to `src/diagrams/rdf/client/`, all in etalii.adp.ide.standalone.

Sources, as read on 2026-09-30:

- The standalone implementation on `develop` of etalii.adp.ide.standalone (commit `b2a2692`): the `Owl/` folder of the RDF module's backend, the family's shared providers (`RdfContextActionProvider.cs`, `RdfContextPropertyProvider.cs`, `RdfSelection.cs`, `RdfValidator.cs`), the client's `OwlCanvas.tsx`, `owl.css` and `register.ts`, the `api/rdf.proto` messages, the examples, the unit and integration tests, `docs/tools.md` line 138, `docs/screenshots/readme.md` and `tests.md`.
- The approved spec-workflow specification `owl-diagram` (requirements, design and tasks), removed from the tree by commit `53f68611` and read from its parent. Requirement numbers below (R1.1 and so on) are that specification's. It built on the anchor specification `rdf-diagram`, whose shared machinery is described in [w3c-rdf.md](w3c-rdf.md).
- The Notion "Tools" database row "OWL ontology": purpose, why specialized, family and rarity. Its page body is blank.
- This project's conversations from 2026-09-26 to 2026-09-30. One user ruling touches OWL directly: the label trim moved onto the shared text metric (Peter, 2026-09-27, section 7). The screenshot on the site was captured in standalone PR #105 (2026-09-28). The general rulings that apply are the `.dis` extension (Peter, 2026-09-30) and one DISL file per standalone tool in `definitions/diagrams/`.

## 1. What the tool is for

An OWL ontology diagram shows the schema an ontology file asserts: its classes and their hierarchy, its properties between their domains and ranges, its restrictions and set operators, and the individuals the same file declares. It is one of four readings of the same Turtle bytes in standalone's RDF module (`w3c/rdf`, `w3c/owl`, `w3c/skos`, `w3c/shacl`), and it shows what the file says, never what a reasoner would add. The definition's description says so in the reader's terms: "An OWL 2 ontology's classes, hierarchy, properties and restrictions - what the file asserts, not what a reasoner would infer." (`Diagram.cs:38`; a test asserts the word "asserts", `OwlSession.Tests.cs:264-278`).

Catalogue data (Notion "Tools" row, `docs/tools.md` line 138): kind Diagram, origin `w3c/owl`, family "Ontologies & semantic web", extensions `.ttl` and `.nt`, rarity "Adoption from standard", theory "W3C OWL 2 overview", state ✅ Implemented in standalone. One-line purpose: "Explore an OWL 2 ontology's classes, hierarchy and restrictions as a VOWL-style graph." Why specialized: "OWL axioms are dense in Turtle or RDF/XML; the VOWL notation shows classes, properties and restrictions so an ontology can be checked by eye." The catalogue row's notes add "classes, hierarchy, restrictions and axioms in the VOWL vocabulary, asserted-only; an RDF reading over the `w3c/rdf` engine" and record that VOWL's old home `vowl.visualdataweb.org` has lapsed, so the notation is cited from the Semantic Web Journal paper and the WebVOWL deployment. Standalone's icon is `mdi-shape-outline`. The screenshot `owl.png` shows PROV-O (`docs/screenshots/readme.md` line 47): "PROV-O's classes as VOWL circles with property edges between them, fitted and then zoomed in twice so the labels read".

The research behind the drawing rules (requirements, "How OWL ontologies are visualized"):

- **Adopted:** VOWL's structural vocabulary (circle classes, rectangle datatypes, dotted subclass edges, labelled property edges, doubled border for equivalence, set-operator nodes, characteristics as words in the property label, dimmed external and deprecated elements, `owl:Thing` anchoring domain-less properties), because it is the one notation in the family with a written specification and several implementations; datatypes as nodes, because in an ontology the datatype is the structure being communicated, while an individual's literal values stay rows on its card; and the asserted class tree as the layout, Protégé's everyday view, arranged by subclass depth with roots on the left.
- **Rejected:** VOWL's force-directed layout (non-deterministic, rejected for the whole family); VOWL's fixed colour palette ("an identity, not a semantics"; `owl.css` lines 6-8 repeat the reason); inline rendering of arbitrarily nested class expressions (nesting is capped instead); and the UML mapping of OWLGrEd and Graffoo (a publication-figure tradition, and two notations at once would serve neither).

## 2. The file and the shared engine

The model file is the ontology's own Turtle or N-Triples, read and written only by the RDF family's shared engine: one parser, one store per file, one history per project root, byte-identical round trips, and edits as minimal splices with byte-restoring undo. That engine, the splice discipline, the drawn-element budget and the reload lifecycle are described once, in [w3c-rdf.md](w3c-rdf.md); this reading owns no parser, store, writer or command class (`Owl/OwlProjection.cs:5-6`; design, "This reading adds zero splice code"). The `.dis` names the engine as the plugin `net.etalii.adp.w3c.turtle`, declared identically in all four readings; this reading uses three of its CEL functions for its dialogs and messages (`rdfResolveTerm`, `rdfTermRefusal`, `rdfDisplayName`).

What this reading uses of the engine: the store's `GetOrLoad` and `Changed` (session and providers), the parsed triples (projection, classification, validator), the family display rule and budget constant, the term compressor (row annotations, the rename dialog's default), the family validator (delegated to, section 8), the family selection ids and truncation test, the dialog term resolver, the gesture ids `new:{x},{y}` and `rel:{from}->{to}`, viewport culling, the reloader, and the `RdfLiteralRow` and `RdfTruncationPayload` wire messages (research notes, section 8). Services registered for this origin alone are the element mapper, validator, toolbox provider, session factory, document factory and a second reloader instance (`ServiceCollection.AddRdf.cs:86-101`); the context resolver, action provider and property provider are registered once for the family and carry the OWL behaviour as extra cases (`ServiceCollection.AddRdf.cs:61-65`).

Every reading of one file shares the parsed document and the history, so an edit through `w3c/rdf`, `w3c/skos`, `w3c/shacl` or `w3c/owl` is seen by all (R8.4; `OwlSession.Tests.cs:161-183`; integration test `OwlFlow.Tests.cs:221-258`, where a label edited to "Pizza (round)" through the ontology reading shows in the graph reading). A file that does not parse opens with an empty model, the canvas is empty, the parse error is the one finding, and every edit is withheld.

**New files.** `Owl/OwlDocumentFactory.cs:21-35` writes, in CRLF with a trailing newline:

```turtle
@prefix : <http://example.org/{local}#> .
@prefix owl: <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#> .
@prefix rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .

<http://example.org/{local}> a owl:Ontology ;
    rdfs:label "{baseName}" .

:Thing1 a owl:Class ;
    rdfs:label "First class" .
```

`{local}` is the base name with every character outside ASCII letters, digits, `-` and `_` replaced by `_`, trimmed of `_`, and `untitled` when nothing is left (`OwlDocumentFactory.cs:38-50`). `{baseName}` is inserted into the literal unescaped, so a `"` in a file name would produce broken Turtle; nothing tests this.

## 3. The registration and where positions live

The `.dis` declares `files.mode: "split"` with the model in `{name}.ttl` and the view in `{name}.adp`, `view.store: ["bounds"]`, and `x-adp.claimsBareFiles: false`. What those stand for:

- **Never routed from a bare file.** `w3c/owl` declares the same extensions as the anchor `w3c/rdf` with `SharedExtension: true`; the anchor is not shared, so a bare `.ttl` or `.nt` always opens as `w3c/rdf`, even when its body carries the ontology marker (`Diagram.cs:31-42`; `OwlFlow.Tests.cs:126-131`). This reading is reached only through a registration whose first line is `w3c/owl` (R8.2).
- **Suggested on Add by a textual marker.** Add offers this reading when the body contains `owl:Ontology` or `http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#Ontology`, an ordinal, case-sensitive substring test and deliberately not a parse (`Diagram.cs:43-46`; `OwlSession.Tests.cs:281-289`). It also fires on a comment or literal holding the text, and misses a file that binds the OWL namespace to another prefix label.
- **The registration file.** An `.adp` beside the ontology holds the type line `w3c/owl`, a `body:` header naming the Turtle file, and an optional `layout:` block of `<element id>: <x> <y>` lines, for example `res:http://www.w3.org/ns/prov#Activity: -169.615 808.315` in the showcase copy of PROV-O (`src/examples/diagrams/owl/prov-o/prov-o.adp`). Positions are the element's top-left corner in the module's canvas units; the client sends `position - size/2` from the drag (`OwlCanvas.tsx:427-433`).
- **No registration header is claimed.** The design considered the family's header facility and claimed no word, because no requirement needs reading-specific configuration (design, "Registration header facility"). No code in `Owl/` reads one.
- **Only named terms are stored.** A stored position applies only to ids starting `res:` or `ind:`; entries for `expr:`, `thing:` or `dt:` are ignored even when present (`Owl/OwlLayout.cs:242-256`). Because a class uses the family id `res:{iri}`, it keeps its authored position when the same body is also open as `w3c/rdf`. Nothing positional is ever written into the ontology (R4.1).

## 4. From triples to drawn elements

DISL's metamodel describes elements a user creates. Here every element is computed from the triples by a pure projection, `Owl/OwlProjection.cs`, over a classification pass, `Owl/OwlModelIndex.cs`. Nothing is inferred (R4.1): no subsumption, no equivalence propagation, no typing from domain or range, no classification of individuals, and a class with two asserted parents has exactly two subclass edges.

**Classification** (`OwlModelIndex.cs:57-169`, per role, so one IRI can be in several sets):

- A **class** is an IRI typed `owl:Class` or `rdfs:Class`; the subject, or IRI object, of `rdfs:subClassOf`; an object of `rdfs:domain`; either end of an IRI-to-IRI `owl:equivalentClass` or `owl:disjointWith`; or an IRI member of an `owl:AllDisjointClasses` list. An object of `rdfs:range` is *not* made a class (section 10).
- An **object property** is an IRI typed `owl:ObjectProperty`, `owl:InverseFunctionalProperty`, `owl:TransitiveProperty`, `owl:SymmetricProperty`, `owl:AsymmetricProperty`, `owl:ReflexiveProperty` or `owl:IrreflexiveProperty`; `owl:FunctionalProperty` alone does not count, because it also types datatype properties (`OwlModelIndex.cs:43-50`). A **datatype property** is typed `owl:DatatypeProperty`; an **annotation property** `owl:AnnotationProperty` (classified, never drawn, used only by the validator).
- An **individual** is an IRI typed `owl:NamedIndividual`, or typed by a non-built-in IRI this file knows as a class (second pass, `OwlModelIndex.cs:131-137`).
- A **datatype** is an IRI in the XSD namespace, `rdfs:Literal`, `rdf:langString`, or an IRI typed `rdfs:Datatype` (`OwlModelIndex.cs:197-200`).
- The **ontology header** is the subject of the *first* `rdf:type owl:Ontology` triple; later ones are ignored.
- **Deprecated** means `owl:deprecated` with the lexical form exactly `true`. **Built in** means the `owl:`, `rdfs:`, `rdf:` or `xsd:` namespace (`Owl/OwlVocabulary.cs:64-68`).

**Which nodes exist, and their ids.** Every triple is walked in document order, subject then object; each IRI in those positions gets, independently, a class node (`res:{iri}`), a Thing node when it is `owl:Thing` (always) or `owl:Nothing` (only when classified as a class), a datatype node (`res:{iri}`), an individual card (`ind:{iri}` when the IRI is also a class, else `res:{iri}`) and the header card (`res:{iri}`) (`OwlProjection.cs:47-53, 248-275`). The first role to claim a `res:` id keeps it: an IRI that is both a class and a datatype, or a class and the header, silently draws only the first role (`OwlProjection.cs:277-282`). Only the class and individual pun gets two elements. Later the projection adds a **Thing anchor** per property per missing side (`thing:{property}|domain`, `thing:{property}|range`, displayed "Thing") and a **Literal anchor** per datatype property without a datatype range (`dt:{property}`, displayed "Literal") (`OwlProjection.cs:121, 315-326`). The `.dis` models these as the types `ThingAnchor` and `LiteralAnchor`, outside the named `Term` family.

**What a named node shows.** The display is the first `rdfs:label` in document order in any language, with no language preference; else the prefixed name under the document's own prefixes; else the local name after the last `#` or `/`; else the full IRI (`OwlModelIndex.cs:95-96`; `RdfProjection.cs:206-217`). Every triple with the IRI as subject and a literal object, except `owl:deprecated`, becomes a row `{predicate, value, annotation}` on the IRI's primary node: the header or class node first, else the individual card, else any `res:` node (`OwlProjection.cs:55-76, 330-343`). The annotation is `@lang`, or the compressed datatype when it is not `xsd:string`. `rdfs:label` is therefore also a row, and a punned IRI's rows go to its class, not its card. The header gets one extra row per `owl:imports`, `owl:imports: <full IRI>` (`OwlProjection.cs:90-96`). Individuals wear as badges the display of every non-built-in `rdf:type` object (`OwlProjection.cs:78-88`). **External** is set only on classes and individuals whose IRI is not built in and is never the subject of a triple in this file; datatypes are never external, because "dimming every xsd term would drown the signal" (`OwlProjection.cs:284-288`).

**Edges.** An edge exists only when both endpoint nodes already exist. Its id is `edge:{fromId}|{propertyIri}|{toId}`, with `|1`, `|2` and so on appended for repeats (`OwlProjection.cs:359-371`).

| Relation in the `.dis` | Wire kind | From which triples | Label |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ObjectProperty` | `object-property` | each object property, domains × non-datatype ranges; a side with no drawn node falls back to the property's Thing anchor | property label (below) |
| `DatatypeProperty` | `datatype-property` | each datatype property, domains × datatype ranges, or the Literal anchor | property label |
| `SubClassOf` | `subclass` | `<S> rdfs:subClassOf <O>`, IRI or blank object | none |
| `EquivalentClass` | `equivalent` | `<S> owl:equivalentClass <O>` | none |
| `DisjointWith` | `disjoint` | `<S> owl:disjointWith <O>`, and every pair i < j of an `owl:AllDisjointClasses` list | none |
| `Assertion` | `assertion` | `<S> <p> <O>` with S an individual, p not built in, O drawn as an individual | display of p |
| `References` | `expression` | an expression's fillers and list members | none |

The property label is the display of the property alone, or `{display} ({words})` where the words are the characteristic words in the order their type triples appear, then `inverse of {display of the inverse}` when the property is the *subject* of `owl:inverseOf` (`OwlProjection.cs:348-357`). The words are "functional", "inverse functional", "transitive", "symmetric", "asymmetric", "reflexive" and "irreflexive" (`OwlModelIndex.cs:32-41`). A property with several domains and ranges draws every pair. A stated domain or range whose IRI has no node is dropped silently; the anchor appears only when no stated end has a node (`OwlProjection.cs:310-326`). One datatype node is shared by every property ranging over it.

**What is never drawn:** `rdf:type` as an edge (types are badges, `OwlProjection.cs:12-13`); properties as nodes; `rdfs:subPropertyOf`; annotation property declarations; `owl:imports` targets (named on the header, never fetched); `rdf:first`/`rdf:rest` cells (R3.3); blank nodes that are not the object of `rdfs:subClassOf`, `owl:equivalentClass` or `owl:disjointWith` with a named subject, such as a union as `rdfs:domain`, an `owl:Axiom` reification or a blank individual; literals as nodes; and IRI-valued annotations such as `rdfs:seeAlso` or `rdfs:isDefinedBy`.

**Class expressions** (`OwlProjection.cs:179-210, 373-451`). For every triple with a named subject and the predicate `rdfs:subClassOf`, `owl:equivalentClass` or `owl:disjointWith`, a counter keyed `{owner}|{predicate}` counts every such triple, named objects included; when the object is a blank node, an expression node is built with id `expr:{ownerIri}|{predicateIri}|{ordinal}`. So `:Vegetarian rdfs:subClassOf :Pizza ; rdfs:subClassOf [ … ]` yields `…Vegetarian|…subClassOf|1` (`OwlFlow.Tests.cs:42`). A nested expression is `{parentId}/{childIndex}`, the index counting only blank children in the parent's triple order. The kind is `Operator` when the blank node has `owl:unionOf`, `owl:intersectionOf`, `owl:complementOf` or `owl:oneOf`, else `Restriction`. Fillers of `owl:someValuesFrom`, `owl:allValuesFrom`, `owl:onClass`, `owl:onDataRange`, `owl:hasValue` and `owl:complementOf`, and members of the three list operators, become `References` edges: to a node for the IRI (created as a datatype or, failing that, as a *class*, so an individual named in `owl:hasValue` or `owl:oneOf` draws as a class), or to a nested expression. Literals and built-in non-datatype IRIs are only in the label; `owl:onProperty` is never a reference.

**The identity boundary.** `expr:` ids are "deterministic within this parse, deliberately unstable across edits" (`OwlProjection.cs:180-181`; `Owl/OwlGraph.cs:56-61`): the same bytes give the same ids (`OwlProjection.Tests.cs:143`), and inserting an axiom shifts an ordinal (`OwlProjection.Tests.cs:158`). That is why expressions refuse stored positions and edits (section 6). The `.dis` marks ids `stable: false` and lists the id shapes in a pattern; it cannot say which shapes may be stored.

**Malformed expressions** (R3.5). An expression is malformed when it is not an operator and has no `owl:onProperty` or not exactly one quantifier triple (someValuesFrom, allValuesFrom, hasValue, cardinality, min and max cardinality, and the three qualified forms), when the renderer meets a cycle, or when a list does not end in `rdf:nil` (`OwlProjection.cs:26-31, 376-416`). A bare `[ a owl:Class ]` is malformed and renders `? ?`. The file still opens; the node is marked and the validator reports it.

**Budget.** The projection has a unit-whole cut: nodes are grouped into units (a named node with its expressions; each anchor alone) in document order, and whole units are kept while they fit the budget of 1000; the first unit that does not fit stops the cut (`OwlProjection.cs:212-246`; `OwlProjection.Tests.cs:200-230`). The live session does not use it: it projects without a limit, culls to the viewport and then keeps the first 1000 visible nodes in node order, and shows the banner whenever the whole file projects to more than 1000 nodes (`Owl/OwlSession.cs:164, 187-218`). Edits are withheld by a different test again, the anchor's resource count (`RdfSelection.cs:103-104`). The `.dis` carries `limits.maxElements: 1000` and the banner as a watermark; DISL has no place for either cut.

## 5. Layout

DISL names a layout; it does not define one. The `.dis` names `plugin:net.etalii.adp.w3c.owlDepthColumns` with a `layered` fallback directed left, so that subclass edges, which run from subclass to superclass, put the roots on the left. What the plugin does (`Owl/OwlLayout.cs:66-213`; tests `OwlLayout.Tests.cs`):

- Pure and deterministic, no physics, no randomness; positions are top-left corners.
- The first ontology header sits at (0, 0); classes start below it at the header card's height plus 80, or at 0 without a header.
- The class set is every class or Thing node with a `res:` id. Depth comes from the drawn subclass edges between two of them (edges to expressions are ignored): roots have depth 0, others 1 plus the maximum depth of their superclasses, and a cycle is collapsed to one strongly connected component with one depth (`Owl/OwlClassHierarchy.cs:27-85`). A class sits in column `depth × 530`, where 530 is a lane offset of 250 plus a lane of 190 plus a gap of 90.
- Column 0 keeps document order; deeper columns are ordered by the barycentre of their already-placed parents' rows, parents without a row last, ties by document order.
- Every node that is not a class or an individual (expressions, datatypes, anchors) is a satellite of its owner if that is a class, else of the first class among the ends of its edges; satellites stack in the lane at `x + 250`, `y + 10 + i × 110`. A class owns a slot of `max(130, satellites × 110 + 65)`, so a class with many restrictions pushes the next one down.
- Individuals go in a band 140 below the tallest column, five to a row, the column pitch the widest card plus 60 and the row pitch the tallest plus 50. Anything still unplaced goes in the same kind of band below that.
- Sizes used for layout, culling and overlap equal the client's: shapes 190 × 70, Thing 0.55 of that, cards 220 wide and `30 + (16 if badges) + 16 × rows + 10` high (`OwlLayout.cs:36-63, 219-234`; `OwlCanvas.tsx:37-54`).

The class comment records three rules "found by drawing OWL-Time": a class owns a slot not a row, satellites live in their own lane, and classes are ordered by where their parents sit (`OwlLayout.cs:13-31`). The `.dis` gives the numbers as plugin options and chooses `trigger: "always"` with `respect: "all"`, the nearest reading of "computed every time, stored positions of named terms win". It cannot say that stored positions apply only to some id shapes.

## 6. Interaction

**Toolbox** (`Owl/OwlToolboxProvider.cs:16-42`). Four entries: Class (`mdi-shape-circle-plus`, "A named class. Drop it where it should sit; you will be asked for its name."), Object property (`mdi-ray-start-arrow`, "A property relating individuals to individuals - drawn as an edge once it has a domain and a range."), Datatype property (`mdi-form-textbox`, "A property relating individuals to data values - drawn as an edge to its datatype."), and Individual (`mdi-account-outline`, "A named individual - a member of the classes this ontology describes."). There is no restriction entry, because "a restriction needs a structure no drop can state" (`OwlToolboxProvider.cs:8-11`; R7.1; `OwlProviders.Tests.cs:235`). A drop runs the entry's action with the placement `new:{x},{y}` (`OwlCanvas.tsx:438-439`); the drop point is not stored, so the new element takes its computed place.

**The add dialogs** (`RdfContextActionProvider.cs:245-248, 328-336, 398-404`). Title "Add class", "Add object property", "Add datatype property" or "Add individual", all with the icon `mdi-shape-circle-plus`, the placeholder "IRI or prefixed name", an empty initial value and the button "Add". The value is resolved under the document's own prefixes: a bracketed IRI, anything containing `://`, or a prefixed name. The refusals are "The brackets are empty.", "'{text}' is neither a full IRI nor a prefixed name. Write ex:{text}, or a full IRI." and "The prefix '{prefix}:' is not declared in this file. Declare it first, write the full IRI, or bracket a scheme IRI as <{text}>." (`RdfTermInput.cs:25-55`). Commit writes exactly one triple, `<iri> rdf:type owl:Class`, `owl:ObjectProperty`, `owl:DatatypeProperty` or `owl:NamedIndividual`, as one undo: no label, no superclass, no domain or range, and no class membership for an individual (`OwlProviders.Tests.cs:134-160`). An existing IRI is not refused; the type is appended to its statement. The writer appends `a owl:Class` as a new `;` pair when the subject already has a statement, else a new statement at the end of the file after a blank line (`RdfWriter.cs:47-68`). The `.dis` expresses the class and individual cases as create actions and the two property cases as plugin actions, because a property is not a node.

**The canvas context menu on empty space** offers "Add resource here…" (`mdi-card-plus-outline`) and "Declare prefix…" (`mdi-at`) from the family, and only when the file holds a triple `? rdf:type owl:Ontology` also "Add class here…", "Add object property…", "Add datatype property…" and "Add individual…" (`RdfContextActionProvider.cs:145-167`; `Owl/OwlSelection.cs:124-126`). The toolbox is not gated this way. DISL has no context menu for the canvas background, so the `.dis` carries the four as `for: "diagram"` operations with a plain `enabled` and records the gate as the diagram attribute `ontologyDeclared`.

**Menus on elements.** A named node (`res:` or `ind:`) offers "Rename…" (`mdi-pencil-outline`, F2) and "Remove", which reads "Remove (with {n} statements)" when the IRI is in more than one triple (`mdi-delete-outline`, Delete) (`RdfContextActionProvider.cs:104-119`). DISL labels are static, so the `.dis` says "Remove". An edge that names one existing triple between two `res:` ids offers "Remove statement" (`mdi-vector-polyline-remove`, Delete) (`RdfContextActionProvider.cs:128-143`). That covers subclass, equivalence, disjointness and assertion edges between `res:` ids; it does not cover property edges (no triple backs them), `AllDisjointClasses` pair edges (their predicate id is the class IRI), or edges touching `ind:`, `thing:`, `dt:` or `expr:` ids. Anchors and expressions offer nothing.

**Rename** asks "Rename resource" with the placeholder "New IRI or prefixed name", the compressed IRI as the initial value and the button "Rename"; a target that already names something is refused with "{iri} already names something in this document; renaming onto it would silently merge two resources." (`RdfContextActionProvider.cs:250-253, 338-344`). Commit rewrites every occurrence as one command.

**Remove** runs at once when the IRI is in at most one triple; otherwise it asks "Remove resource", "Removing this resource also removes the {n} statements it appears in.", with a danger button "Remove" (`RdfContextActionProvider.cs:255-271`).

**The subclass gesture** (R6.1). The canvas declares source anchors `axiom-left` and `axiom-right` at the middle of the left and right sides of every named node (class, Thing, datatype, individual, header) and none on any other relation type (`OwlCanvas.tsx:64-100`). A drawn connection always dispatches `owl.subclass` with the `rel:` id, without a menu (`OwlCanvas.tsx:436-437`). The backend requires both ends to be `res:` ids, else "A subclass relation needs two named classes."; refuses an existing triple with "That subclass relation is already asserted; drawing it again would state nothing new." (`OwlSelection.cs:17-18`); and otherwise writes one `rdfs:subClassOf` triple as one undo (`RdfContextActionProvider.cs:222-243`; `OwlProviders.Tests.cs:88, 116`). It does not check that the ends are classes, so a gesture from a datatype or the header would write the triple. The `.dis` restricts the gesture to classes and Things, which is what the specification meant, and lists this as a difference (section 10). The discovery path for a `rel:` gesture offers "Subclass of" (`mdi-file-tree`) when both ends are classes by a third definition (typed, or subject of `rdfs:subClassOf`, or object of `rdfs:subClassOf`, `rdfs:domain` or `rdfs:range`, `OwlSelection.cs:115-121`) and always the family's "Relate…" (`RdfContextActionProvider.cs:169-189`), but the canvas never opens that menu.

**Moving** (`Owl/OwlSession.cs:86-136`). Dragging a named node writes its top-left into the registration's `layout:` block through `SetRegistrationLayoutCommand`, one undo, never touching the ontology (`OwlFlow.Tests.cs:134-184`: a class stored at (420, 260), surviving reopen, undo restoring the `.adp` byte for byte). The refusals, in the order checked, verbatim:

1. "This diagram is read-only." (no history)
2. "This diagram was opened without a registration, so there is nowhere to store a position. Register the file to arrange it."
3. "That element is not something this diagram can move." (an edge, or the truncation banner)
4. "That is an anonymous class expression, whose identity does not survive an edit to the file, so a stored position could not be trusted. It takes its place beside the class that uses it; edit the expression as text." (`OwlFlow.Tests.cs:186-219`; tests.md, 2026-09-05)
5. "That element is drawn where its property needs it and cannot be arranged on its own." (a Thing or Literal anchor)

Dropping onto another element asks to reparent, which is always refused: "An ontology element has no parent to move it under; dragging changes where it sits on the canvas." (`OwlSession.cs:86-94`). The `.dis` carries all six as placement constraints, but cannot say that refusal 3 applies to edges and the banner, which are not placeable in DISL at all.

**Property grid** (`RdfContextPropertyProvider.cs:82-132, 185-274`). Groups are Identity, Documentation and Axioms. For a named node: "IRI" (read-only, "Rename through the context menu, so every reference follows the name."), "Types" (every `rdf:type` object joined with ", ", built-ins included, read-only, "Types are stated by triples; add or remove them as statements."), "Label" and "Comment" (the first `rdfs:label` and `rdfs:comment`, editable unless the view is truncated), then one row per axiom named "Subclass of", "Equivalent to", "Disjoint with", "Domain", "Range" or "Inverse of" and one "Characteristic" row per characteristic word, all read-only with "Axioms are stated by triples; draw or remove them as edges and statements." or, for an expression object, the expression refusal below. A label or comment edit first adds a plain literal triple; later edits rewrite only the literal token, keeping its language and datatype. For an expression: one "Expression" row with the full, uncapped rendering, read-only, "That is an anonymous class expression, whose identity does not survive an edit to the file, so nothing about it can be edited from the diagram. Edit the expression as text." (`OwlSelection.cs:13-14`). For a property edge whose property is explicitly typed `owl:ObjectProperty` or `owl:DatatypeProperty`: the property's IRI, axiom and characteristic rows (`OwlSelection.cs:92-112`); a property typed only by a characteristic class draws but gets no rows. For a plain triple edge: "Predicate", "A statement's predicate is the statement; remove and restate to change it.". The `.dis` gives attributes these names and groups; it cannot carry a separate read-only reason per row, so the reasons sit in the attributes' descriptions.

**Selection text.** The breadcrumb names a node by its display and an edge as "{from} → {to}"; a vanished element reads "That element is no longer in this file." (`RdfContextSourceResolver.cs:81-91, 139`; `OwlSelection.cs:40-71`). An `ind:` id resolves only while a triple with that subject exists; an `expr:` id resolves by projecting again, so after an edit it may name a different expression or nothing.

**Truncation.** Every edit on a truncated view is refused with "The diagram shows only the first part of this file under the drawn-element budget, so edits through it are withheld - an edit through a partial view could touch what the view does not show. Edit the file as text instead." (`RdfSelection.cs:21-22`), and the banner reads "Showing {shown} of {total} elements — edits are withheld on this truncated view" (`OwlCanvas.tsx:469-473`).

**Viewport delivery.** A connection receives only the nodes whose box meets its viewport, plus nodes without a position, capped at 1000, and the edges whose ends both travel (`OwlSession.cs:187-218`; `RdfViewport.cs:25-42`). tests.md (2026-09-05) records an open defect: Fit to View fits to the delivered subset, so on OWL-Time the drawn set fell from 114 nodes to 85 and stayed there.

## 7. Notation the `.dis` approximates

The standalone canvas is a declarative definition rendered by the central canvas library (`OwlCanvas.tsx:112-363`, `owl.css`). Where DISL's notation is close but not exact:

- **Ellipses, not circles.** VOWL's circle is drawn as a 190 × 70 ellipse for classes and expressions, and every class is the same size; VOWL's sizing by instance count is not used (`OwlCanvas.tsx:26-27`).
- **The double ring.** An element touched by any `equivalent` edge, as source or target, is drawn with the library's `double-ellipse`: a second ellipse 4 inside the first, with its own stroke class (`OwlCanvas.tsx:399-405, 499-507`; `DiagramCanvas.tsx:3247-3260`). Both ends of an equivalence are doubled, including an expression; boxes and cards have no doubled form. The `.dis` approximates the second ring with `stroke.double.gap: 4`. VOWL's single merged circle carrying both names (R2.2) is not implemented.
- **owl:Thing** is a dashed (`4 3`) ellipse at 0.55 of a class's size, 104.5 × 38.5, for a stated `owl:Thing`, for `owl:Nothing` and for every anchor. The inner ring of a doubled Thing is not dashed.
- **Expressions** are dashed `3 2` ellipses with 11 px labels. Their text is DL-style symbols, not Manchester keywords (`Owl/ExpressionRenderer.cs`): `∃ p.C`, `∀ p.C`, `∋ p.v`, `= n p`, `≥ n p`, `≤ n p`, the qualified forms with `.C` from `owl:onClass` or `owl:onDataRange`, `(A ∪ B)`, `(A ∩ B)`, `¬A`, `{a, b}`, a missing part as `?`. The first quantifier triple in document order wins. On the canvas the rendering is capped at depth 2 (`CanvasDepth = 2`), deeper structure reads `…` and the drawn label gets a trailing " …"; a revisited blank node reads `…` and marks the expression malformed. The grid and the axiom rows use the uncapped rendering. Test examples: capped `∃ :p.(:B ∪ …)` against uncapped `∃ :p.(:B ∪ ∀ :q.(:C ∩ :D))`, and malformed `∃ ?.:B`, `? :p`, `? ?` (`ExpressionRenderer.Tests.cs:31-110`). The `.dis` keeps the rendered text as attributes the plugin fills; DISL has no recursive text renderer over a model structure.
- **Cards.** Individuals and the header are 220-wide boxes whose height follows their content: a 30 title band with the title at y 20, a 16 badge line at y 40 (badges joined with " · ", 11 px, primary colour), then one 16 row per literal ("{predicate}: {value} {annotation}", 11 px, muted), then 10 padding (`OwlCanvas.tsx:192-287, 402`). The `.dis` uses a label for the badges and a compartment for the rows.
- **Class rows are not drawn.** Classes carry literal rows on the wire, but the ellipse draws only the name; rows show on cards and in the grid.
- **Dimming.** Deprecated and external elements both draw at opacity 0.55; nothing tells them apart on the canvas (`owl.css:66-69`). A malformed expression's outline takes the warning colour (`owl.css:72-74`).
- **Edges** are straight, 1.5 wide in the muted text colour. Subclass is dashed `6 4` with an arrow (VOWL's dotted line with its "Subclass of" label became a dashed arrow); equivalence is a solid 2-wide line without a marker; disjointness is a dotted `1 5` line with round caps and no marker (VOWL's dedicated symbol is not drawn); expression references are dashed `2 3` at opacity 0.7; property and assertion edges have an arrow and their label 6 above the midpoint (VOWL's borderless label rectangles are plain text). Cardinalities appear only in expression labels, never on property edges (`owl.css:77-93`; `OwlCanvas.tsx:85-100`).
- **Label fitting and the shared text metric.** Labels are cut to their shape with an ellipsis by the library's fit, using the one client text metric: characters × font size × 0.55, at the label's own font size (12 by default, 11 for expressions, badges and rows), with 8 kept free inside the outline (`src/client/src/canvas/label/textMetrics.ts`; `labels.ts:428-446`). The OWL canvas used to trim at its own 6.2 px per character; on 2026-09-27 Peter ruled "Move it" when asked "Bring the OWL canvas's own label trimming onto the shared fit?", accepting that OWL labels lose about a character on long names, and chose "Backend everywhere" for the metric itself. The client-centralization specification was amended the same day (requirements 4.1 and 12.1, design section D), and PR #71 ("one text metric, the backend's") landed it, with a guard that fails on any width constant outside the shared file. The exported helpers `labelFor` and `fit` in `OwlCanvas.tsx:478-496` still exist and use the same metric with 16 kept free, but the drawing does not call them. The full text is always the tooltip. The `.dis` says `overflow: "ellipsis"`; DISL has no way to name the metric.
- **Colours** are standalone's theme variables, copied as tokens in the `.dis`: surface `#ffffff`/`#1e293b`, border `#e2e8f0`/`#334155` (every OWL outline), text `#0f172a`/`#f1f5f9`, muted `#64748b`/`#94a3b8` (edges and rows), warning `#b45309`/`#fbbf24`, primary `limegreen` (badges). No hex colour appears in the OWL styling itself.
- **The truncation banner** is an HTML box above the surface: 8 px from the top, centred, `4px 12px` padding, a 1 px warning-coloured border with radius 4, surface background, warning text at 12 px (`owl.css:96-108`). The `.dis` approximates it with a canvas watermark.
- **Icons.** Only the definition icon (`mdi-shape-outline`) and the toolbox icons exist; no icon is drawn on an element. The icons on the `.dis` node types are for palettes and forms only.
- **CSS hooks.** Each element carries `owl-node canvas-element owl-{kind}` plus `owl-deprecated`, `owl-external`, `owl-malformed` and `owl-elided` when they apply; `owl-elided` has no rule. Standalone's "no stylesheet rule without an emitter" guard mounts the canvas on the shipped examples (`src/fixtures/cross-tier/example-models/showcase-owl.json`) to check the classes.

## 8. Validation

`Owl/OwlValidator.cs` first runs the family validator for this origin and, if the file does not parse, returns only its finding; otherwise it appends its own. Every finding is on a 1-based line.

| Rule id (standalone) | Severity | Message (verbatim template) | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rdf.unparseable` | error | "This is not RDF that can be read: {reason}" | the parse error's line |
| `rdf.duplicate-prefix` | warning | "The prefix '{p}:' is declared more than once; from here on it means {iri}, which changes what every earlier-styled use would say." | the redeclaration |
| `rdf.relative-iri` | warning | "This document uses relative IRIs but declares no base, so their meaning depends on where the file happens to sit. Declare an @base." | the first such triple, once |
| `rdf.language-tag` | warning | "'@{tag}' is not a well-formed language tag (letters, then optional '-' groups of letters and digits)." | the literal |
| `rdf.unknown-datatype` | warning | "xsd:{name} is not a datatype XSD defines; tools that check will refuse the value." | the literal |
| `owl.subclass-cycle` | warning | "These classes assert each other as subclasses in a cycle: {names}. That is legal OWL - it makes them mutually equivalent - and it is almost always a mistake." | the first `rdfs:subClassOf` triple whose subject is in the cycle |
| `owl.malformed-expression` | error | "This class expression is not well-formed: it renders as '{display}', with ? standing for what the structure is missing." | the first triple of the expression's root blank node, else line 1 |
| `owl.undeclared-property` | info | "{display} is used as a property but declared nowhere in this file - it may live in an import, which is deliberately not fetched." | its first use |
| `owl.deprecated-reference` | info | "{display} is deprecated, and something not deprecated still references it." | the first such reference |
| `owl.imports-not-fetched` | info | "This ontology imports {full IRI}, which is not fetched: the diagram shows what this file asserts, not the import closure a reasoner would load." | each `owl:imports` triple |

(`OwlValidator.cs:22-175`; `RdfValidator.cs:21-136`; `OwlClassHierarchy.cs:88-153`; tests `OwlValidator.Tests.cs:24-127`.)

- DISL constraints run over a model and attach to elements; these findings attach to *lines of the ontology text*. A parse failure has no place in DISL at all; the `.dis` leaves all five family rules and the replacement rule to the Turtle plugin, as the SKOS specification does.
- **Cycles** are found by Tarjan's algorithm over IRI-to-IRI subclass triples, one finding per cycle (and one per self-loop), naming its members by prefixed or local name, never by `rdfs:label`. The `.dis` rule is scoped to a class, so a DISL runtime reports one finding per member; the `.dis` names members with `rdfDisplayName` for the same reason.
- **Undeclared property** checks the subject of `rdfs:domain`/`rdfs:range` and the object of `owl:onProperty`; a property declared only as `rdf:Property` or only as `owl:FunctionalProperty` counts as undeclared. It is reported once per IRI. Properties are not elements, so the `.dis` reports them through the diagram attribute `undeclaredProperties` as one diagram-level message.
- **Deprecated reference** counts any triple other than `rdf:type` and `owl:deprecated` whose IRI object is deprecated and whose subject is a blank node or a non-deprecated IRI, drawn or not. The `.dis` carries that count as `liveReferences`, which the plugin fills in.
- **Imports** are reported for every `owl:imports` triple with any subject, not only the header's, and not deduplicated. The `.dis` rule sits on the header.
- **Malformed expressions** include nested and cyclic ones, and `{display}` is the depth-capped label.
- Not validated: `rdfs:subPropertyOf` cycles, domains or ranges that are not classes, individuals typed by undeclared classes, a missing `owl:Ontology`, or several of them (the first silently wins).
- OWL-Time's readme says it "opens with no validation findings" although deprecated classes are still referenced there, which would raise `owl.deprecated-reference` infos; the requirement it answers (R9.3) said "zero validation findings above info level", which is the likely meaning.

## 9. Out of scope, by decision

- **Inference.** No reasoner, no inferred hierarchy, no classification; the definition's description, the catalogue row and the imports finding say so where a reader sees it (R4).
- **Fetching.** `owl:imports` is named, never followed; nothing touches the network (R4.2; family no-network rule).
- **Editing class expressions.** Restrictions and set operators are read-only on the canvas and in the grid; editing them is text work, and no restriction toolbox entry exists (R3.2, R6.5, R7.1).
- **Expanding elided expressions on the canvas.** An expanding node would need stored per-element state, which the identity boundary rules out; the grid shows the full text instead (design, "Elision, and the third level").
- **VOWL's palette and physics, and UML notations** (section 1).
- **A registration header** (section 3).
- **Other serializations.** RDF/XML, OWL/XML, Manchester and functional syntax are not read; the family engine reads Turtle and N-Triples only, which is why the pizza ontology was not vendored (section 11).

## 10. Where the implementation and its specification differ

Recorded so a port to another IDE knows which one to follow. Where the `.dis` had to choose, it follows the implementation unless stated.

1. **Range objects are not classes.** R1.1 makes every object of `rdfs:range` a class; the index adds only domain objects (`OwlModelIndex.cs:101-107`). A range class declared nowhere else has no node, so the property falls back to a Thing anchor on that side. The subclass-gesture discovery does count range objects as classes (`OwlSelection.cs:120-121`), so the two definitions of "class" disagree.
2. **External.** R1.6 says "an IRI outside the ontology's own namespace, used but not declared here"; the code says "never the subject of a triple here, not built in, and only for classes and individuals" (`OwlProjection.cs:286-288`). The namespace plays no part.
3. **Equivalence.** R2.2's doubled border "both names legible" is a double ring on each end plus a separate solid edge; the two classes are not merged into one shape.
4. **Disjointness groups.** `owl:AllDisjointClasses` expands to n(n-1)/2 pairwise edges; there is no group marker and no dedicated symbol (R2.2; `OwlProjection.cs:167-177`).
5. **Sub-properties.** R2.3 requires `rdfs:subPropertyOf` to appear; it appears nowhere (the constant in `OwlVocabulary.cs:19` is unused). `owl:inverseOf` labels only the subject side.
6. **Punning.** R2.4 requires the grid to name the pun; no row does, and a punned IRI's literal rows go to its class rather than its card.
7. **Expression syntax.** R3.1 and the design call the labels Manchester-style; they are DL symbols (`∃ ∀ ∋ = ≥ ≤ ∪ ∩ ¬ { }`), and `owl:hasValue` is `∋` rather than `value`.
8. **Nesting.** R3.4 asks that levels beyond two render as one elided node; the label is capped at two levels, but every nested expression is still drawn as its own node at every depth (`OwlProjection.cs:438-446`).
9. **Domain and range gestures.** R6.2 wants stating a domain or range to be its own gesture; none exists. Only the family "Relate…" with a typed predicate could write one, and the canvas never offers it. The subclass action does not check that its ends are classes (`RdfContextActionProvider.cs:222-243`); the `.dis` restricts it to classes and Things.
10. **Grid rows.** R7.2 is met (axiom rows with uncapped text). R7.3's "types and assertions" for an individual is met only as Types, Label and Comment; assertions are not listed, and no class lists the properties that point at it.
11. **Truncation.** R8.3 measures the budget against this reading and keeps class neighbourhoods whole; the unit-whole cut exists but the live session culls by viewport and takes the first 1000 visible nodes, and edits are withheld by the anchor's count (section 4; `OwlSession.cs:179-186` explains why the viewport approach replaced "first-N").
12. **Design data model.** The design's `instance-of` edge and "imports as badges on the header" do not exist (types are badges on individuals, imports are header rows); the expression payload gained a `kind` field (`restriction`/`operator`) the design did not have (`api/rdf.proto`).
13. **Layout.** The design said "within a column, document order", "datatype nodes beside the domain class" and "a cycle at its minimum depth"; the code orders by barycentre, puts satellites in the lane of the first connected class and gives a collapsed cycle one component depth (`OwlLayout.cs:128-176`).
14. **Examples.** R9.1 and R9.3 named the pizza ontology and a Gene Ontology extract; neither is vendored (documented), and deep nesting is covered by unit tests only.
15. **Annotations.** R1.4 wants annotations in the element's rows and the grid; classes carry rows the ellipse never draws, and the grid shows only Label and Comment, not `owl:versionInfo`, `skos:*` or `dct:*`.
16. **Label language.** The first `rdfs:label` in document order wins whatever its language; the specification set no rule.
17. **Two marker tests.** Add's suggestion is a text search; the canvas menu's OWL actions are gated on a parsed `rdf:type owl:Ontology` triple.
18. **Toolbox and menu disagree.** A file registered as `w3c/owl` without the marker gets no OWL add actions in the canvas menu, while the static toolbox still lists them and a drop still works.
19. **Properties without nodes.** A declared property with neither domain nor range still draws, between two private Thing anchors; an annotation property never draws; characteristics are visible only in edge labels and property-edge rows.
20. **owl:Nothing** is drawn like `owl:Thing`, small and dashed (`OwlProjection.cs:257`).
21. **First writer wins.** An IRI that is both a class and a datatype, or a class and the header, silently draws only the role met first (`OwlProjection.cs:277-282`).

## 11. Examples

Real, published ontologies, vendored under the family's rule (licence verified at acquisition, `LICENSE.md` beside the data, provenance readme), in `src/diagrams/rdf/examples/` and copied to the showcase at `src/examples/diagrams/owl/`:

- **`owl-time/`**: "Time Ontology in OWL", W3C Recommendation 19 October 2017, fetched from `https://www.w3.org/2006/time` as Turtle on 2026-09-04 and unmodified. Licence CC BY 4.0, stated in band as `dct:license`, with the attribution "OWL-Time, W3C Recommendation 19 October 2017. Copyright © 2006-2017 W3C, OGC. Editors: Simon J D Cox and Chris Little." carried in `LICENSE.md`. It exercises 54 restrictions, a union, two enumerations, disjointness, deprecated classes still referenced and 14 named individuals; as drawn, 114 elements, 144 axiom edges, 55 expression nodes, 17 datatype nodes, 2 dimmed deprecated classes and 1 dimmed external term. tests.md (2026-09-05) confirms ellipses and boxes, labels such as `∀ days du…` and `≤ 1 month`, and `January` and `Year` dimmed at 0.55.
- **`prov-o/`**: "PROV-O: The PROV Ontology", W3C Recommendation 30 April 2013, `https://www.w3.org/ns/prov-o.ttl`, retrieved 2026-09-04 and unmodified. Licence: the W3C Software and Document License, reasoned in `LICENSE.md` because the file carries no licence triple. 39 classes, their hierarchy, properties with domains and ranges, 8 unions, 4 disjointness axioms and one restriction; as drawn, 42 elements and 83 axiom edges. The showcase copy's registration carries 24 authored positions; the module copy carries none. The site's screenshot is taken from it.
- **Deliberately absent:** the pizza ontology (published upstream only as RDF/XML, and no converter is in the toolchain, so a hand conversion would be a provenance nobody could check) and any over-budget ontology (the permissive candidates are OBO releases in RDF/XML); the unit-whole cut is covered by unit tests only (examples `readme.md`).
- **Test fixtures:** `Fixtures/owl-ontology.ttl`, a pizza-style corpus covering a header with imports, labels and `owl:versionInfo`, subclass, disjointness, deprecation, restrictions, a named and a nested equivalence, characteristics and `owl:inverseOf`, properties with and without domains and ranges, individuals with literal and object assertions, punning, `owl:AllDisjointClasses` and an external class; and `Fixtures/owl-malformed.ttl`, a restriction without `owl:onProperty`.

## 12. What DISL 0.1 could not say, in short

For whoever takes DISL to 0.2:

1. **Several readings of one model file.** Four specifications read one Turtle file through one shared engine, store and history, and a bare file routes to one of them only. DISL has one specification per file type; the `.dis` falls back on a shared plugin and `x-adp` keys.
2. **Elements derived from triples.** Every element is computed by classification and projection; DISL has derived attributes and relations, but no derived nodes, and no way to say that one IRI yields two elements (punning) or that the first role claims an id.
3. **Edges that are not triples.** A property edge is the property itself, drawn once per domain and range pair, with anchors materialized for missing ends.
4. **Anonymous structure with unstable identity.** Expression ids are deterministic within a parse and unstable across edits; DISL can mark ids unstable but cannot say which id shapes may be stored, positioned or edited.
5. **A recursive text renderer.** The DL-style expression text with its depth cap and cycle guard is a function over graph structure, not a CEL expression over attributes.
6. **Findings on text lines,** a parse failure as a finding, and one finding per cycle rather than per member.
7. **Refusal sentences per gesture and element kind,** a read-only reason per property row, and a label that counts ("Remove (with {n} statements)").
8. **A context menu on empty canvas** gated on a model fact, separate from the toolbox.
9. **Layout interplay:** stored positions honoured for some id shapes and ignored for others, and satellites placed relative to an owner.
10. **Budget behaviour:** a unit-whole cut, a viewport cap and an edit-withholding test that each count differently, where DISL has only a soft `maxElements`.
11. **A named text metric** for fitting labels, which a user ruling fixed as characters × font size × 0.55.
